verdict: Amplemarket is a strong AI outbound platform with a high price floor and weak CRM-pipeline fit. Review based on first-party research, not hands-on testing.
strengths: Lead intelligence via Searcher and intent signals
weaknesses: Not a CRM pipeline system of record
Startup floor at $600/mo annual is expensive
bestFor: Outbound-led B2B teams investing in AI multichannel engagement
Sales orgs already on HubSpot/Salesforce needing an engagement layer
Teams that will use Growth/Elite CSM packaging
notIdealFor: Solo users who only need contact lookup
Teams unwilling to manage mailbox/domain deliverability
tradeoffs: Outbound automation depth vs CRM completeness
AI breadth vs high subscription floor
Published Startup price vs custom Growth/Elite quotes
recommendation: Choose Amplemarket when AI multichannel outbound is the job-to-be-done and $600+/mo is acceptable. Keep a CRM for pipeline; compare Apollo/Closely for lighter motions.
editorialNotes: Approved from live Amplemarket pricing/product/integration pages. handsOnTesting=false.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Product marketing emphasizes guided Duo assistants and unified inbox; still an advanced outbound suite rather than a simple CRM.
Amplemarket orchestrates outbound; deal pipelines stay in CRM systems like HubSpot/Salesforce.
AI multichannel engagement / sequences are the Amplemarket job — stronger automation than a contact-DB peer.
Mailbox sync, Unibox, deliverability tooling, and AI copywriting are first-class.
Dedicated Analytics product for outbound performance monitoring.
Sequences/workflows/integrations are flexible; not an enterprise CRM customization canvas.
Salesforce/HubSpot plus Zapier/Clay/HTTP and mailbox providers are prominently documented.
Deliverability, domains, and seat/contact packaging imply meaningful RevOps overhead.
Growth/Elite raise contacts/seats with CSM; contact pools scale to 400k on Elite.
Startup at $600/mo annual is a high floor; Growth/Elite custom — strong only if unit economics of outbound justify it.

overallScoreRationale: Equal-weight CRM methodology average. Automation/email/integrations pull up; pipeline and price floor pull down.
